verdicts.evidence: L3: "description: Fills validation gaps by generating real behavioral tests ... Dispatched by the orchestrator/pipeline after verifier produces VERIFICATION.md's validation_gaps list."
verdicts.reasoning: KICKOFF L919 verified verbatim: '*(only if verify reported validation gaps — and only after integration-checker has returned)*'. This is a dispatch-time gate the operator judges before the agent exists as a running process; a frontmatter description is documentation of provenance, not enforcement, and an agent that is never invoked cannot enforce its own invocation precondition. The second half — ordering relative to integration-checker — is absent from the skill entirely (grep for 'integration' returns only Test Type table rows at L65/L67 and the return-template cell at L133; grep for parallel|concurr|sibling|alongside|sequential|wait returns nothing). Load-bearing, KEEP. Severity low because the gaps-exist half is at least paraphrased at L3.

verdicts.evidence: L14: "**Implementation files are READ-ONLY.** Only create/modify: test files, fixtures, `VERIFICATION.md`'s `validation_gaps` entries (path configurable by the orchestrator). Implementation bugs → ESCALATE. Never fix implementation."
verdicts.reasoning: Verified verbatim at L14. The KICKOFF sentence is a near word-for-word transcription of the skill's own <role> hard rule — same bolded 'read-only', same allow-list opening (test files, fixtures), same 'ESCALATE, never a fix' terminal clause. It is redundantly re-enforced three more times in the skill: L102 ('Assertion: actual matches impl but violates requirement | IMPLEMENTATION BUG → ESCALATE'), L191 ('Implementation files never modified'), L193 ('Implementation bugs escalated, not fixed'). High severity is justified beyond mere length: the guide's allow-list drops the skill's third permitted target, VERIFICATION.md's validation_gaps entries, so an operator reading only the guide would believe the agent may not update the verification map it is explicitly chartered to update. Lossy restatement, not just duplication.
